note: These are gaps in the G.14.11 text. The G.14.12 documents state the missing rule. That is design text. It is not a measured control. Implementation stays blocked for every item.

defects.g14_11_gap: Ancestor chain was required and not specified
defects.evidence: G.14.11 receiving filesystem note said ancestors were not enumerated. G.14.8 cases 1-3 show a writable parent is enough.
defects.scenario: The interactive user replaces one ancestor before the receiver's CreateFileW. Children are created in the substitute.
defects.remediation: filesystem_ancestor_trust_contract.md denies write, delete, WRITE_DAC, and WRITE_OWNER on every ancestor. No path is approved.

defects.g14_11_gap: Executable, configuration, and import paths were not placed
defects.evidence: A separate SID does not bind bytes the interactive user can replace
defects.scenario: The user replaces the interpreter or a module. The receiver process loads the substitute.
defects.remediation: receiver_executable_integrity_review.md puts the program, runtime, config, and logs on the same chain and discards the user environment.

defects.g14_11_gap: Pipe authentication order, squatting, and impersonation were incomplete
defects.evidence: G.14.11 required SID checks and did not order them. No pipe exists.
defects.scenario: The user creates the pipe first, or connects as a client, and the other side trusts the name.
defects.remediation: authenticated_transfer_contract_review.md requires server-SID then client-SID then nonce, and forbids ImpersonateNamedPipeClient.

defects.g14_11_gap: Transfer maximums were deferred without a refusal rule
defects.evidence: An absent maximum could have been read as unlimited
defects.scenario: A sender streams without a cap and the receiver stores it.
defects.remediation: If the approved configuration has no count or byte maximum, fail closed before the first body is stored. The number is not invented here.

defects.g14_11_gap: Publication could be read as file-id plus hash after the handle closed
defects.evidence: NTFS file indexes can be reused after deletion. G.14.8 post-open binding does not survive a later path open.
defects.scenario: The object is deleted, a new object reuses the index, and a consumer opens a path.
defects.remediation: publication_mutation_review.md requires a commit on the open handle, a re-read before send, and no consumer path open.

defects.g14_11_gap: Consumer program and launch method were unnamed
defects.evidence: receiver_to_build_contract.md authenticated the receiver and did not place the consumer binary
defects.scenario: The consumer executable is user-writable, or a service path is swapped.
defects.remediation: The consumer binary and any launch configuration must sit on the same chain. No launch method is selected. Until one is approved, the receiver is not started.

defects.g14_11_gap: Privilege set for the receiver token was not listed
defects.evidence: Current token privileges are not the receiver's
defects.scenario: The receiver account is created with backup or take-ownership rights and can rewrite unrelated objects.
defects.remediation: The receiver token must be non-administrator and must not hold SeDebugPrivilege, SeImpersonatePrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege, SeRestorePrivilege, SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege, SeTcbPrivilege, or SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege.

defects.g14_11_gap: Whether this interactive account can elevate
defects.evidence: Administrators is deny-only on this token. No elevation was attempted.
defects.scenario: A later elevated process rewrites the receiver DACL.
defects.remediation: Threat C is outside the claim. The contract does not need a UAC result to be internally stated, and it must not be described as administrator-proof.
